texts.facts: ' 1. This is a suit for permanent and mandatory injunction for restraining infringement of trade mark, copyright, passing off delivery up accounts for profit and damages. 2. In brief facts of the case are that plaintiff is a proprietorship firm engaged in the business of manufacturing and selling JUICE under the inherent distinctive trade name "HONEY JUICE" which is duly registered on 18.05.2016 vide Trade mark number 3261664 under Trade Mark Act 1999. It is submitted that in the year 2015, plaintiff got the licence from the Department of Food Safety under FSS Act, 2006 for manufacturing and selling of JUICE in the name of "HONEY JUICE and that the label HONEY JUICE is to be used on packing pouch which primary consist of the distinctive features are as under:- a) The packing pouch primarily a transparent which consists of label "HONEY JUICE" Shri Pawan Kumar vs Shri Israruddin on 31 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113354080/ 1 in the front portion of pouch. b) The label on the packing pouch is being divided in various panels whereby, in a panel, the trade mark "HONEY JUICE is being represented in a special and particular manner, being inscribed in a distinctive panel. c) In the remaining portion of pouch the descriptive matter inscribed and written in transparent background. d) In the packing pouch, juice is being stored inside the packing pouch and a host of the various fruit images are printed on such pouch in the white colour ink in typical and distinctive front and style. 3. It is further the case of plaintiff that aforesaid work is an original work of the plaintiff having distinctive feature and arrangement and representative of slogan/ text/panel/design gate up and layout depicted in a special and particular manner, as such the plaintiff being the lawful owner prior and exclusive user of the aforesaid trademark claim under the provision of the Trade Mark Act 1999. The purchasing public particularly semi-literate and illiterate people identify the said product of the plaintiff from the said label comprising of distinctive features. It is stated that the aforesaid trade mark "HONEY JUICE" including the said distinctive label thereof by virtue of its prior long, continuous, extensive and exclusively has become distinctive and same is associated exclusively with the name of the plaintiff by trade as well as the purchasing public. 4. It is urged that the aforesaid product of the plaintiff under the said trade mark "HONEY JUICE" under the pouch sold on extensive sale and on an exclusive basis throughout the republic of India and that plaintiff has been expending huge amount of the sale promotion activities through various means and modes to promote the popularize the aforesaid trade mark "HONEY JUICE" and its label in respect of aforesaid product as such the said product is owned by the plaintiff and carned a wide recognization, unique goodwill and reputation amongst the trade as well as purchasing public. That it is submitted that recently the plaintiff have came across a product which looks identical product manufactured and supplied by the plaintiff. It is stated that after examination it is revealed that the said product sold in the market is not the product of the plaintiff and is being manufactured and supplied by the defendant No. 1 under the trade name of the plaintiff i.e. "HONEY JUICE" and that the said product is of inferior quality. 5. It is further the case of plaintiff that upon enquiries the plaintiff also came to know that the other persons including defendants No. 2 to 4 are selling the juice product under the name and style of "HONEY JUICE", which on the face of it tantamount to infringement of trade mark counterfeiting a property mark and using a false mark which is registered under the name of "HONEY JUICE". It is submitted that upon going through the said product, plaintiff also came to know that the defendants have adopted and started using and infringing mark on their infringed product. It is stated that to this effect plaintiff made a complaint to the S.H.O. PS Sangam Vihar, Mangal Bazar Road, Block D, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi on 28.03.2018 for registration of FIR against the defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 1 had given the undertaking before S.H.O. PS Sangam Vihar and stated that it is running the business under the name of "HONEY JUICE" and not having any licence and in future it will not manufacture under the name and style of "HONEY JUICE". However, despite this, defendant No. 1 is manufacturing and selling the product under the name and style of "HONEY JUICE" and supplying to other defendants No. 2 to 4 and other persons also who are selling the produce manufactured by the defendant No. 1. It is stated that the parties to the suit are reside and work of gain within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court and hence this Court has the jurisdiction to entertain and decide the present suit. 12. Plaintiff has prayed for passing a decree of permanent injunction in terms of which the defendant No. 1 including defendants No. 2 to 4 and other persons with their employees, agents, representatives, stockists, distributors, be restrained from using or incorporating the trade name of "HONEY JUICE" on the product. It is further prayed that defendant No. 1 including his employees, associates, agents, distributors, representative be restraining by means of injunction from stocking the items. Summons of the suit were issued to defendants and in pursuance of summons, on 06.09.2018, defendant no. 1 had appeared and vakalatnama of Shri Randhir Kumar, counsel had been filed on behalf of the said defendant no. 1. Defendant no. 1 filed his written statement on 21.02.2019. Defendant No. 4 had appeared on 01.12.2018 and sought time for filing written statement. However, thereafter defendant no. 4 has not appeared in the court. Defendant no. 2 and 3 had failed to appear despite service of summons and they were, therefore, proceeded exparte vide order dated 01.12.2018 15. Plaintiff has filed replication to the written statement of defendant no. 1 and reiterated his version as claimed in the suit. To prove its case, plaintiff examined himself as PW-1 on 27.09.2019. On 23.01.2020, this case was received in this court by way of transfer from the court of ADJ- 02 . On that day itself ,HC Raj Kumar was examined as PW-2 and on 13.02.2020, Shri Sunil Kumar Chaturvedi, Local Commissioner was examined as PW-3 & plaintiff closed his evidence . 21. PW-1 has tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A and placed on record copy of certificate issued by Trademark Registry Ex.PW-1/1; copy of title Honey Juice Ex.PW-1/2; copy of licence issued by Department of Food Safety under FSS Act, 2006 Ex.PW-1/3; original package pouch of plaintiff Ex.PW-1/4; original package pouch of defendants Ex.PW-1/5; legal notice dated 21.03.2018 issued to defendant no. 1 as Ex.PW- 1/6; its postal receipt Ex.PW-1/7; copy of complaint dated 28.03.2018 filed before PS Sangam Vihar Ex.PW-1/8 and copy of undertaking given by defendant before PS Sangam Vihar Ex.PW-1/9. 22. PW-2 HC Raj Kumar has deposed that complaint Ex.PW-1/8 dated 28.03.2018 is purported to have been received by SI Veer Singh and complainant might have given this complaint directly to SI Veer Singh. PW-3, Shri Sunil Kumar Chaturvedi, advocate has deposed that vide order dated 29.05.2018 of Ld. Predecessor of this court, he was appointed Local Commissioner in the present matter to inspect the premises of defendant no. 1 and pursuant to said order he had inspected the premises of defendant no. 1 on 02.06.2018 after taking the police aid and thereafter he had submitted his report in the court on 06.06.2018. This witness has tendered in evidence his report alongwith annexures as Ex.PW-3/A and has also proved photographs Ex.PW-3/P-1 to Ex.PW-3/P-29. PW-3 has also proved site plan, Ex.PW-3/P- 30 and seizure memo Ex.PW-3/P-31. 24.

It is stated that defendant no 1 has not infringed the trade mark "HONEY JUICE" or by any agents etc. whereas he is manufacturing and selling his product as "HONEY" and that the label placed on record are quite different, on the face of it Label of defendant no. 1 printed with picture of bubbles of water whereas the label of the plaintiff printed with the picture of lemon. It is contended that defendant no 1 has no intention to counterfeit or copy trade mark of the plaintiff as label of defendant no 1 product are very distinct from the product of the plaintiff. It is stated that it is also clearly mentioned on the label of the defendant no 1 product that the product has manufactured by Rukhsar Food Products New Delhi. 16. It is further contended that the product is containing juice or extract of juice, that's why defendant no 1 mentioned on the back panel of the it's label as juice and that in the label of the product of the defendant no 1, it is written in Hindi "Cheeni wa Neemboo ke tatav se bana", whereas the label of product of plaintiff printed with the picture of lemon/fruits. It is contended that defendant 1 named their product as per the ingredients' of the product and defendant no 1 has not infringed the trade mark licenses available to the plaintiff. It is stated that the trade mark licenses available with the plaintiff is "HONEY JUICE", whereas the defendant no. 1 manufacturing the product as "HONEY. It is stated that plaintiff has filed the present suit just to harass the defendant competitors as to establish his monopoly in the market of his own product. Defendant No. 1 has denied that defendant no 1 manufactured and supplied under the trade name of the plaintiff i.e. "HONEY JUICE". It is also denied by defendant no. 1 that his product is of inferior quality and that the product of the defendant. No. 1 is not safe for the human consumption. It is also denied by defendant no. 1 that there is no difference between the pouches which are being used by the plaintiff and infringing label pouch. Defendant no. 1 has also denied that he has used the goodwill and reputation of the plaintiff and he is manufacturing and sale under the name of HONEY JUICE. It is also denied that the defendant no 1 infringes label of pouch of HONEY JUICE and that defendant no 1 tainted and malafide intension to create the confusion and deception amongst the trade purchasing public. 17. Defendant No. 1 has stated that he is a illiterate person and by the hands and gloves of the police official, plaintiff compel to write in the police station that he will not manufacture and sell the products in the name of HONEY JUICE. It is submitted that suit of the plaintiff may be dismissed with heavy cost. has deposed that his aforesaid product under the said trade mark HONEY JUICE under the pouch sold on extensive sale and on an exclusive basis throughout the republic of India. Learned counsel for the plaintiff submits that Trademark "HONEY JUICE" adopted by the defendant is deceptively similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark and plaintiff is prior user and has adopted with registration well known "HONEY JUICE" Trademarks and this will erode the distinctiveness and value associated with the trademark of the plaintiff and the defendants intended to portray incorrect facts on the website and this fact of defendants amounts to abuse in plaintiff's well known Trademark and will cause irreparable loss, harm and injury to the plaintiff by causing confusion and deception in the mind of the innocent public and consumer. It will cause harm to the reputation of high quality of goods & services being provided by the plaintiff. It is submitted that in case of registered trademark, court has to compare word "HONEY JUICE" and Trademark/Trade name only and nothing else. Counsel for the plaintiff has further submitted that as per LC report Ex.PW-3/A, at the time of inspection small empty pouches of HONEY JUICE were seen in one open bag and liquid was flowing in the drain 1 bag with filled pouches having HONEY JUICE was also lying there. Pandit Durga Dutt Sharma vs Navaratna Pharmaceuticals Laboratories MANU/SC/0197/1964. Legal position is well settled that the Courts adjudicate trade mark disputes applying the test of similarity/deceptive similarity, and which test has to be in relation to how similarity/deceptive similarity is perceived in the minds of the concerned persons and not on paper. 31. The case of the plaintiff is that defendants are using trade mark 'HONEY JUICE' which are deceptively similar trademark of the plaintiff and harming the reputation of the plaintiff. Apart from causing monetary loss to the plaintiff. It is submitted that upon going through the said product, plaintiff also came to know that the defendants have adopted and started using and infringing mark on their infringed product. It is urged that the product manufactured and sold by the defendant is without any authority as the product is not containing any mark of FSSAI, which also submitted that the defendant No. 1 has not taken any licence from the department of Food Safety under FSSAI Act 2006 and the product manufactured and sold by the defendants are not safe for human consumption. 34. It is submitted that the defendant No. 1 has adopted and infringing label, on packing pouch of the identical/similar product and business so as to trade upon the establish goodwill and reputation of the plaintiff with respect to his aforesaid original and prior use label and to undue profits in an Shri Pawan Kumar vs Shri Israruddin on 31 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113354080/ 9 illegal and unauthorized manner which further amounts to unfair trade practice. 35. Plaintiff has further stated that it had issued a legal notice dated 21.03.2018 to the defendant No. 1 through his counsel Shri Sumil Bindal and the said notice was duly served upon the defendant No. 1 but the defendant did not care of the said legal notice neither stopped his illegal acts nor taken any action against the illegal sellers. It is submitted that on account of illegal and unauthorized acts of the defendants in passing of the goods with the name of "HONEY JUICE" will directly and adversely effects the cause irreparable loss prejudice and damage to the goodwill and reputation of the plaintiff in the market built up entirely due to the hard work of the plaintiff. 36. It is further submitted that defendants are further likely to destroy the plaintiff brand and market in case of quality of the defendants product deficient, inferior and substandard and that on account of illegal, unlawful and nefarious acts on the part of the defendant No. 1 and other persons including other defendants No. 2 to 4 has caused a great deal of loss and injury to the goodwill, reputation and loss of business opportunities due to the sale marketing of the material. is urged that on account of loss of business, goodwill reputation, the plaintiff assess his damages to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- which the defendant is liable to pay for unauthorized and unwarranted use of trade "HONEY JUICE". 37. Ld. Counsel has argued that plaintiff caused loss for his reputation and goodwill as such the business is on the bank of close of his business. It is further submitted that intention of the defendant No. 1 is not good towards the plaintiff. 40. Onus to prove this issue was on the plaintiff.
